blocks.raw: ## Payment File Upload | new status values in file upload API
blocks.text: Payment File Upload | new status values in file upload API

blocks.raw: We are making changes to the file upload processing flow for the Payment File Upload service. As part of this update, the `GET /payment-file-upload-service/payment-files/{fileId}` endpoint will return two new status values that you may observe when polling for file status.
blocks.text: We are making changes to the file upload processing flow for the Payment File Upload service. As part of this update, the GET /payment-file-upload-service/payment-files/{fileId} endpoint will return two new status values that you may observe when polling for file status.
What's changing

blocks.raw: **PROCESSING**- your file has been picked up and is actively being validated. This is not a terminal state; you should continue polling until a final status is returned.
blocks.text: PROCESSING- your file has been picked up and is actively being validated. This is not a terminal state; you should continue polling until a final status is returned.

blocks.raw: **ERROR\_RETRYABLE**- a system error occurred during processing. This is a terminal state; you should retry the upload.
blocks.text: ERROR_RETRYABLE- a system error occurred during processing. This is a terminal state; you should retry the upload.

blocks.raw: Also note: the `POST /payment-file-upload-service/payment-files` endpoint now returns a 500 in two additional scenarios: an object store failure or a queue publish failure during the upload phase. In either case, no pollable file record is created, so a 500 from this endpoint always means the upload did not go through and should be retried.
blocks.text: Also note: the POST /payment-file-upload-service/payment-files endpoint now returns a 500 in two additional scenarios: an object store failure or a queue publish failure during the upload phase. In either case, no pollable file record is created, so a 500 from this endpoint always means the upload did not go through and should be retried.

blocks.raw: If you are handling status values exhaustively in your integration, make sure to account for these additions to avoid unexpected failures.
blocks.text: If you are handling status values exhaustively in your integration, make sure to account for these additions to avoid unexpected failures.
What you need to do

blocks.raw: Review your integration against the updated status lifecycle and ensure your polling logic handles the two new values. For full API reference, see <https://modulr.readme.io/reference/upload-payment-file>
blocks.text: Review your integration against the updated status lifecycle and ensure your polling logic handles the two new values. For full API reference, see https://modulr.readme.io/reference/upload-payment-file
API
Direct Debit Indemnity Claim (DDIC)

blocks.raw: To improve visibility of Direct Debit Indemnity Claims (DDIC), we are introducing a webhook to notify incoming claims and status changes.
blocks.text: To improve visibility of Direct Debit Indemnity Claims (DDIC), we are introducing a webhook to notify incoming claims and status changes.

blocks.raw: This webhook will be available for new claims from **June 30th** and supplements your existing DDIC process.
blocks.text: This webhook will be available for new claims from June 30th and supplements your existing DDIC process.
What’s changing:

blocks.raw: The new webhook `DD_INDEMNITY_CLAIM_STATUS` triggers whenever a claim changes status:
blocks.text: The new webhook DD_INDEMNITY_CLAIM_STATUS triggers whenever a claim changes status:

blocks.raw:
1. NEW - a claim has been raised against your account. You have until working day 9 to challenge it via the BACS Payment Service Website (PSW).
2. CANCELLED - Customer successfully challenged the claim. No settlement will occur.
blocks.text: NEW - a claim has been raised against your account. You have until working day 9 to challenge it via the BACS Payment Service Website (PSW).CANCELLED - Customer successfully challenged the claim. No settlement will occur.

blocks.raw: SETTLED - the claim amount has been debited from the customer’s collateral account (14 working days after initial advice). The settlement entry now includes the service user reference for easier reconciliation.
blocks.text: SETTLED - the claim amount has been debited from the customer’s collateral account (14 working days after initial advice). The settlement entry now includes the service user reference for easier reconciliation.

blocks.raw: Claim status can be checked on demand using two new endpoints:
blocks.text: Claim status can be checked on demand using two new endpoints:
GET/direct-debit-service/indemnity-claims
and
GET/direct-debit-service/indemnity-claims/{id}.
Action required:

blocks.raw: Review API documentation and subscribe to the `DD_INDEMNITY_CLAIM_STATUS` webhook to receive notifications.
blocks.text: Review API documentation and subscribe to the DD_INDEMNITY_CLAIM_STATUS webhook to receive notifications.

blocks.raw: **Reminder:** Direct Service Users’ authorised contacts can challenge a DDIC via the [BACS Payment Services Website (PSW)](https://paymentservices.bacs.co.uk/online/newbacs/loginBrowser.do?dts=0E9BED9F5D7D95F1CD9BFD47421E8A6F598371ED) up to working day 9. For customers where Modulr is the Service User (FM-DD), challenges must be processed through Modulr support.
blocks.text: Reminder: Direct Service Users’ authorised contacts can challenge a DDIC via the BACS Payment Services Website (PSW) up to working day 9. For customers where Modulr is the Service User (FM-DD), challenges must be processed through Modulr support.
